title: Residue modules, semilinear constant maps, and local tensor generation
statement: For the coefficient data of [def-weil-pbc-completed-constant-realization-data], equip N/I^k N with its natural A/I^k action and define multiplication by sections of the constant quotient ring sheaf. Evaluation of a completed scalar determines its action on this quotient. Construct sheafified semilinear maps of constant modules compatible with specified scalar maps; compute them on constant generators and their underlying additive sheaves. Maps from a scalar-extended constant module are determined by pure tensors of completed scalars and actual constant module elements. A semilinear identity on one additive group identifies its two constant-module scalar actions through the induced map of constant ring sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03EK and Tags 093J--093M; quotient scalar actions, sheafified scalar extension, and the explicit tensor-to-limit map

proof.text: Construct constant-module semilinear maps by module sheafification. Naturality of the ring sheafification unit proves scalar compatibility, and the sheafification universal property computes the maps on generators and their underlying additive sheaves. A semilinear identity has identity underlying constant additive-sheaf map, so its scalar-linearity identifies the two constant scalar actions.

A completed scalar with zero k-th evaluation belongs to I^k C by the evaluation-kernel theorem. Its product with a module element belongs to I^k N. This gives the evaluation-semilinear residue map and its quotient action.

To compare maps from scalar extension, first use the underlying sheafification unit and tensor induction. For a pure tensor, restrict along the covering image sieve of the constant-module sheafification unit, on which the module element has an actual constant representative. Separatedness then proves equality. Restriction of raw tensors is computed by the existing scalar-extension tensor API.
